items.q: The protocol on this page begins with:
items.exp: Protocol: confirm diagnosis of CKD. (Book p807)

items.q: For a patient fit for transplant, the hurdle listed on the page is:
items.exp: If patient fit for transplant: hurdles — vascular complications (medial calcifications) → ↓ chance of success. (Book p807)

items.q: Vascular complications with medial calcifications improve the chance of a successful transplant.
opts: False — they lower the chance of success
False — they are irrelevant to transplant
items.exp: Hurdles for transplant: vascular complications — medial calcifications → ↓ chance of success. (Book p807)

items.q: The transplant-success ranking written on the page is:
items.exp: Success: CGN, CTID > DKD, IN. (Book p807)

items.q: A CKD patient with chronic glomerulonephritis is being compared with one with diabetic kidney disease for transplant. Per the page, the better expected transplant success belongs to:
items.exp: Success: CGN, CTID > DKD, IN. (Book p807)

items.q: The dialysis-mortality co-relation graph plots mortality rate against:
opts: Days after the start of dialysis
Serum creatinine at the same time point
The GFR measured at the time of admission
Urine albumin excretion over the same period
items.exp: Graph: mortality rate* vs days after the start of dialysis (0-360). (Book p807)

items.q: On that graph, the mortality-rate curves sit at their highest during which window?
items.exp: Mortality rate peaks early (≈34% at day 15-50 in age >65; ≈22-23% all patients) and falls over the 360-day course. (Book p807)

items.q: Which curve sits lowest on the dialysis-mortality graph throughout the 360 days?
items.exp: The age <65 curve runs lowest (≈6-7% early, ≈2% by day 350); age >65 runs highest (≈34% early). (Book p807)
